newsitem.title: UK: Finnish wage hikes should be kept low - Hamalainen.
newsitem.headline: Finnish wage hikes should be kept low - Hamalainen.

text.p: Finland should not allow wages to rise too fast in good times and increases in 1997 should be kept at very low levels, Sirkka Hamalainen, governor of the Bank of Finland, said in an interview with Central Banking magazine.

"Above all, Finland must not let wages rise to fast in good times and undermine our competitiveness again. It will be essential in the 1997 wage agreement to keep wage rises to very low levels," Hamalainen said.
She said both nominal and real wages could be more stable. "We should not let nominal wages rise too fast, we must strengthen the reserves and financial strength of our corporate sector," she said.
Finland's unemployment rate is one of Europe's highest and the country's thorniest problem.
Hamalainen said Finland's unemployment, like much of Europe's, was due to high taxes and indirect labour costs.
"Income taxes are very high even on very low incomes. Then you have VAT and very high social security contributions based on wages and salaries. This creates disincentives to work," she said.
